key_insight: NeFTY represents 3D thermal diffusivity as a continuous neural field and couples it with a differentiable transient heat solver so that surface temperature measurements can be inverted to yield accurate, quantitative 3D material property maps while accounting for lateral diffusion.
problem_solved: Conventional thermography treats each pixel as a 1D problem (ignoring lateral heat spread) and soft-constrained PINNs struggle with transient diffusion (gradient stiffness), producing poor or non-quantitative reconstructions. NeFTY addresses robust, quantitative 3D reconstruction of material properties from transient surface temperature data for non‑destructive evaluation.
method: Parameterize the 3D thermal diffusivity field as a continuous neural field (neural network representation).
Integrate a differentiable transient heat-diffusion forward model so surface temperature predictions are differentiable w.r.t. the neural field for end-to-end inversion.
Employ training/stabilization strategies tailored to transient diffusion (e.g., multi-scale/time weighting and solver-aware differentiation) to overcome gradient stiffness and improve convergence.
impact: Provides a practical, scalable recipe for combining neural fields with differentiable physics to solve diffusion-based inverse problems—enabling more accurate, quantitative non‑destructive evaluation and offering a template for other physics-driven ML applications.
visual_elements: Schematic pipeline: neural field → differentiable heat solver → simulated surface temps → loss/backprop to update field (loop diagram).
3D volume rendering: reconstructed diffusivity field vs ground truth (side-by-side) to show quantitative accuracy.
Time-series surface temperature plots: measured vs NeFTY-predicted to illustrate fit across transient windows.
Comparison panel: results of NeFTY vs pixel-wise 1D thermography and standard PINN (error maps / quantitative metrics).
paper_title: Neural Field Thermal Tomography: A Differentiable Physics Framework for Non-Destructive Evaluation
paper_authors: Tao Zhong, Yixun Hu, Dongzhe Zheng, Aditya Sood, Christine Allen-Blanchette
